statement: The function returns a result r and r equals the number of k with 0 <= k < 26 satisfying all three conditions: (1) there exists i with 0 <= i < len(word) and word[i] = L_k; (2) there exists j with 0 <= j < len(word) and word[j] = U_k; and (3) for every i and j with 0 <= i < len(word), 0 <= j < len(word), if word[i] = L_k and word[j] = U_k then i < j. Here L_k = 97 + k and U_k = 65 + k.
preconditions: len(word) is an integer with 1 <= len(word) <= 200000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(word), word[i] is an ASCII byte in 97..122 (lowercase English letter) or 65..90 (uppercase English letter).

statement: For every word satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail, overflow, go out of bounds, or panic.
preconditions: len(word) is an integer with 1 <= len(word) <= 200000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(word), word[i] is an ASCII byte in 97..122 (lowercase English letter) or 65..90 (uppercase English letter).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= 26.
preconditions: len(word) is an integer with 1 <= len(word) <= 200000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(word), word[i] is an ASCII byte in 97..122 (lowercase English letter) or 65..90 (uppercase English letter).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is at most the number of k with 0 <= k < 26 for which both L_k = 97 + k and U_k = 65 + k occur at least once in word.
preconditions: len(word) is an integer with 1 <= len(word) <= 200000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(word), word[i] is an ASCII byte in 97..122 (lowercase English letter) or 65..90 (uppercase English letter).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and len(word) = 1, r = 0.
preconditions: len(word) is an integer with 1 <= len(word) <= 200000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(word), word[i] is an ASCII byte in 97..122 (lowercase English letter) or 65..90 (uppercase English letter).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if there is no index i with 0 <= i < len(word) and 97 <= word[i] <= 122, then r = 0.
preconditions: len(word) is an integer with 1 <= len(word) <= 200000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(word), word[i] is an ASCII byte in 97..122 (lowercase English letter) or 65..90 (uppercase English letter).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if there is no index i with 0 <= i < len(word) and 65 <= word[i] <= 90, then r = 0.
preconditions: len(word) is an integer with 1 <= len(word) <= 200000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(word), word[i] is an ASCII byte in 97..122 (lowercase English letter) or 65..90 (uppercase English letter).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if for every k with 0 <= k < 26 such that both L_k = 97 + k and U_k = 65 + k occur in word, there exist indices i and j with 0 <= i,j < len(word), word[i] = U_k, word[j] = L_k, and i < j, then r = 0.
preconditions: len(word) is an integer with 1 <= len(word) <= 200000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(word), word[i] is an ASCII byte in 97..122 (lowercase English letter) or 65..90 (uppercase English letter).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if for every i and j with 0 <= i,j < len(word), whenever 97 <= word[i] <= 122 and 65 <= word[j] <= 90 we have i < j, then r equals the number of k with 0 <= k < 26 for which both L_k = 97 + k and U_k = 65 + k occur in word.
preconditions: len(word) is an integer with 1 <= len(word) <= 200000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(word), word[i] is an ASCII byte in 97..122 (lowercase English letter) or 65..90 (uppercase English letter).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r > 0 if and only if there exists k with 0 <= k < 26 such that both L_k = 97 + k and U_k = 65 + k occur in word and for every i and j with 0 <= i,j < len(word), if word[i] = L_k and word[j] = U_k then i < j.
preconditions: len(word) is an integer with 1 <= len(word) <= 200000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(word), word[i] is an ASCII byte in 97..122 (lowercase English letter) or 65..90 (uppercase English letter).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 26 if and only if for every k with 0 <= k < 26, both L_k = 97 + k and U_k = 65 + k occur in word and for every i and j with 0 <= i,j < len(word), if word[i] = L_k and word[j] = U_k then i < j.
preconditions: len(word) is an integer with 1 <= len(word) <= 200000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(word), word[i] is an ASCII byte in 97..122 (lowercase English letter) or 65..90 (uppercase English letter).

statement: Suppose that for every i with 0 <= i < len(word), word2[i] is obtained from word[len(word)-1-i] by swapping ASCII case: if word[len(word)-1-i] is in 97..122 then word2[i] = word[len(word)-1-i] - 32, and if word[len(word)-1-i] is in 65..90 then word2[i] = word[len(word)-1-i] + 32. Then whenever the function returns r on word and r2 on word2, r = r2.
preconditions: word and word2 are byte arrays with lengths in 1..200000, len(word2) = len(word), and every byte of each is a lowercase or uppercase English letter.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if there exists k with 0 <= k < 26 such that every byte of word is either L_k = 97 + k or U_k = 65 + k, then r = 1 if both L_k and U_k occur in word and for every i and j with 0 <= i,j < len(word), if word[i] = L_k and word[j] = U_k then i < j; otherwise r = 0.
preconditions: len(word) is an integer with 1 <= len(word) <= 200000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(word), word[i] is an ASCII byte in 97..122 (lowercase English letter) or 65..90 (uppercase English letter).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for each k with 0 <= k < 26 let lastL(k) be the largest index i with word[i] = L_k = 97+k, if it exists, and let firstU(k) be the smallest index j with word[j] = U_k = 65+k, if it exists. Then r equals the number of k for which both lastL(k) and firstU(k) exist and lastL(k) < firstU(k).
preconditions: len(word) is an integer with 1 <= len(word) <= 200000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(word), word[i] is an ASCII byte in 97..122 or 65..90.

statement: Whenever the function returns r on word and r2 on word2, if the appended byte is an uppercase letter U_k, then r2 >= r; if the appended byte is a lowercase letter L_k, then r2 <= r.
preconditions: word and word2 are byte arrays with lengths in 1..200000, every byte is a lowercase or uppercase English letter, len(word) < 200000, len(word2) = len(word)+1, word2[i] = word[i] for 0 <= i < len(word), and word2[len(word)] is either U_k = 65+k or L_k = 97+k for some k with 0 <= k < 26.
